text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
---Financial regulators are study large business loans moved from one bank to another this year to ensure that banks are pursuing sound loan policies.
---Upmarket TV and HiFi manufacturer Bang & Olufsen has appointed a new international marketing director, a signal that it intends to pursue a more consistent marketing policy.
--- Shipping group A.P. Moeller unit, airline company Maersk Air, plans to compete against SAS on its most lucrative route -- between Copenhagen and Stockholm.
--- The government has agreed new laws against organised crime, including raising the penalty for carrying weapons to up to four years in prison.
--- More Danes are saving with investment associations, which by now have more than 50 billion crowns of private savings, an increase of 35 percent from last year.
--- Textile dyers are launching an offensive to counter imports, stressing the environmental consciousness of local production.
